If these changes are severe, minor fish kills are possible below the dam during these periods, to some undetermined point downstream where oxygen, temperature, etc., recover enough to maintain aquatic life. Fish can acclimatize themselves to many different environmental conditions, and with daily operation of this facility this problem will probably be very minor and then only limited to the immediate tailrace area. However, this situation is limited to degrees of change that aquatic life could normally adjust to, and not to extremes that are toxic and will not support aquatic life. Weirs located below the dam at 2.2 and 12.6 miles should add significant dissolved oxygen on the basis of their obvious aeration potential as visually observed during an approximated 4,000 cfs test release. Also, during this release, which could approximate conditions of hydropower operation except for modeling dissolved oxygen, the temperature recovered to "normal" about 9 miles below the dam.

4.37 Lake Falcon Fishery. The addition of the hydroelectric plant at Amistad Dam will not detract from the program to maintain reservoir levels as stable as possible during the fish spawning periods. Amistad hydro-releases will be adjusted to have Falcon Reservoir inflows about the same as its outflows during the spawning period at Falcon. During the spawning period at Amistad, the hydro-releases will be adjusted to the inflows to the extent possible.
4.38 The stable water levels should enhance largemouth bass spawning in the spring by inundating shoreline vegetation. This will provide ample nesting areas and allow the fry better protection from predators. This will also release nutrients in the soil and indirectly benefit food organisms for the game fish young. The flooding of littoral areas will also provide additional zones for benthic production. This stabilization will induce strong year classes of game fishes and improve the ratio of game to nongame fishes in the lake.
4.39 Recreational aspects, especially fishing, will benefit from these temporary stabilized water levels. Better access to inclinities and the lake will be afforded. Fishing success should also be better due to the expanding population of game fishes.
4.40 Benthos. Project operation should have a minimal effect on benthic populations in Amistad Reservoir and the Rio Grande. The largest populations are found in the littoral areas of the lake associated with the vegetation and bottom: sediment. The mobility of most benthic species would allow them to adjust location to lake water level changes.
4.41 The hypolimnion discharges during operation should not have an adverse effect on downstream benthos. The only area of concern is the immediate area of discharge. Here the substrate is scoured, rocky, and not very conductive to benthos production. These releases may increase riffle areas downstream, thus possibly increasing benthos productivity.
